    3. Deep Dive: Subject-Specific Variances for Missing Covariates

    Part3-deep-dive-subject-specific-variances-for-missing-covariates.Rmd

    Introduction

    The FFEM conversion normally derives one set of variance parameters and gives it to every subject. That assumes everyone carries the same covariate information. Where covariates are missing, and missing in different combinations from subject to subject, the assumption does not hold: a subject whose weight was never measured should keep the variability that weight would have explained, while a subject with a full covariate record should not.

    omegaToData = TRUE relaxes it. Each subject gets the variance-covariance matrix implied by their own missing-covariate pattern, carried in the data set rather than in $OMEGA.

    1. How it works

    The matrix a subject is given is the FREM covariance conditional on the covariates that subject actually has. Since it differs between subjects it cannot live in $OMEGA, which is estimated once for the run. Instead the elements travel in the data set, and the model rebuilds the correlated random effects from them through a Cholesky factorization of the individual matrix \(V\):

    \[V = L L^{T}\]

    \(L\) is lower triangular, so independent standard normal ETAs become correlated MYETAs by

    \[L_{ii} = \sqrt{V_{ii} - \sum_{k<i} L_{ik}^{2}}, \qquad L_{ij} = \frac{V_{ij} - \sum_{k<j} L_{ik} L_{jk}}{L_{jj}}\]

    The indices are the model’s own eta numbers, so in a model with skipped omegas they start above them: run31 skips two, and its FREM parameter etas are 3, 4 and 5.

    2. The data set

    createFFEMdata(omegaToData = TRUE) appends one column per element of the lower triangle, named for the etas it belongs to.

    library(PMXFrem)

modDevDir <- system.file("extdata/SimNeb", package = "PMXFrem")
td <- tempdir()

ffem <- createFFEMdata(
  modName     = "run31",
  modDevDir   = modDevDir,
  parNames    = c("CL", "V", "MAT"),
  dataFile    = file.path(modDevDir, "DAT-2-MI-PMX-2-onlyTYPE2-new.csv"),
  newDataFile = file.path(td, "ffem_omegaToData.csv"),
  omegaToData = TRUE,
  quiet       = TRUE
)

vCols <- grep("^V[0-9]+$", names(ffem$newData), value = TRUE)
vCols
#> [1] "V33" "V43" "V53" "V44" "V54" "V55"

    numNonFREMThetas and numSkipOm are not passed: the model is located through modName / modDevDir, so they come from the model and its .ext via fremModelInfo(). V33 is the variance of eta 3, V43 its covariance with eta 4, and so on.

    The values differ from subject to subject:

    firstRow <- ffem$newData[!duplicated(ffem$newData$ID), ]
head(firstRow[, c("ID", vCols)], 4)
#>    ID        V33        V43         V53        V44        V54        V55
#> 1   1 0.06632247 0.02009448 0.006784914 0.05275882 0.02383014 0.04556839
#> 14 13 0.06568269 0.02023636 0.005403792 0.05272841 0.02413118 0.04261320
#> 27 19 0.14878568 0.10245971 0.007276704 0.13446721 0.02555877 0.04312456
#> 40 25 0.14808621 0.10230700 0.006663042 0.13443387 0.02542479 0.04258617

    They differ because the covariate records differ. Subject 19 is missing one covariate more than subject 1, and keeps a larger unexplained variance on clearance:

    covs <- getCovNames(file.path(modDevDir, "run31.mod"))$orgCovNames
covs <- intersect(covs, names(firstRow))

nMissing <- function(id) sum(firstRow[firstRow$ID == id, covs] == -99)

data.frame(
  ID              = c(1, 19),
  covsMissing     = c(nMissing(1), nMissing(19)),
  varianceOnCL    = firstRow$V33[firstRow$ID %in% c(1, 19)]
)
#>   ID covsMissing varianceOnCL
#> 1  1           2   0.06632247
#> 2 19           3   0.14878568

    3. The model code

    createFFEMmodel(omegaToData = TRUE) fixes the FREM part of $OMEGA to an identity matrix and writes the factorization into $PK, reading the V-columns from the data set.

    ffemMod <- createFFEMmodel(
  runno       = 31,
  baserunno   = 30,
  modDevDir   = modDevDir,
  parNames    = c("CL", "V", "MAT"),
  dataFile    = file.path(modDevDir, "DAT-2-MI-PMX-2-onlyTYPE2-new.csv"),
  newDataFile = file.path(td, "ffem_omegaToData_model.csv"),
  ffemModName = file.path(td, "run31_omegaToData.mod"),
  omegaToData = TRUE,
  quiet       = TRUE
)

    The generated $PK block:

    i <- grep("Cholesky factors", ffemMod)
cat(ffemMod[i:(i + 21)], sep = "\n")
; 1. Cholesky factors (L) for an 3x3 matrix
;    (Offset applied: starting at index 3)
; ----------------------------------------------------------------

; Column 3
L33 = SQRT(MAX(0.000001, V33))
L43 = V43 / L33
L53 = V53 / L33

; Column 4
L44 = SQRT(MAX(0.000001, V44 - L43**2))
L54 = (V54 - L53 * L43) / L44

; Column 5
L55 = SQRT(MAX(0.000001, V55 - L53**2 - L54**2))

; ----------------------------------------------------------------
; 2. Multiply standard ETA with L for correlated MYETA
; ----------------------------------------------------------------
MYETA3 = L33 * ETA(3)
MYETA4 = L43 * ETA(3) + L44 * ETA(4)
MYETA5 = L53 * ETA(3) + L54 * ETA(4) + L55 * ETA(5)

    And the $OMEGA records the factorization replaces. The two skipped omegas are untouched; the FREM block is an identity matrix, fixed:

    j <- grep("^\\$OMEGA", ffemMod)[1]
cat(ffemMod[j:(j + 6)], sep = "\n")
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) 
0.0541999 
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) 
1e-04
$OMEGA BLOCK(3) FIX
1.0
0.0 1.0

    4. When to use it

    omegaToData = TRUE is worth the extra columns when the covariate record is incomplete and the gaps are uneven - a subject missing four covariates and one missing none should not share a variance. With a complete covariate record every subject gets the same matrix, and the default omegaToData = FALSE says the same thing with less machinery.
